consequence.statement: Argo CD will now ignore `.status` updates and known high churn changes by default, which may change synchronization and monitoring behavior compared to the previous release.

original.statement: By default, Argo CD 3.0.0 ignores `.status` updates and known high churn changes, a change from previous behavior.

decision.reason: [ev-45214d096bc9] says only that Argo CD now ignores all `.status` updates and known high-churn changes by default. The commit is marked breaking ("!"), but the evidence never says anything fails, is rejected or stops being honoured. A new default that keeps working is behavior-change, so review class is right and a mandatory-work kind would over-claim. The proposed statement hedges its wording ("may change") and stays within what the evidence supports. Confidence is low because the changelog line does not say exactly which reconciliation or monitoring behaviour is affected.
